jl-03-gafanhoto.context: Joel opens the book with a plague that devours the land in a chain. Before any explanation, the people are called to hear what happened and tell the generations to come.
jl-03-gafanhoto.focusQuestion: When losses pile up in your life, do you usually stop to hear what God wants to show you in them?
jl-03-gafanhoto.keywordGloss: One of the chain of devourers in Joel 1:4; each eats what the one before left.
facts: The word of the Lord came to Joel, son of Pethuel.
The people must tell what happened from generation to generation.
What the caterpillar left, the locust ate.
A mighty and countless nation came against the land.
The vine was ruined and the fig tree withered.

jl-04-coracao.context: Facing the Day of the Lord, Joel does not ask for a gesture to impress. The invitation is to return to God with all your heart, because he is merciful and slow to anger.
jl-04-coracao.focusQuestion: What outward gesture have you used in place of a sincere return of the heart to God?
jl-04-coracao.keywordGloss: The center of the person; it is the heart, not clothing, that Joel says to tear before God.
reflectionPrompts: The heart, not just the garment
facts: Before him the earth quakes and the sun and moon grow dark.
The Day of the Lord is great and very terrible.
God calls them to return to him with all their heart.
Joel says to tear the heart and not the garments.
God is slow to anger and abounding in love.
In Zion the trumpet must sound and a solemn fast be proclaimed.

jl-05-anos.context: After the devastation, God promises life back in the field, rain in due measure and years restored. The restoration ends in praise and in God's presence among the people.
jl-05-anos.focusQuestion: What lost year would you hand over to God today, trusting that he can restore what was eaten?
jl-05-anos.keywordGloss: God's promise to give back to the people the years the plague ate, with plenty and praise.
facts: The wilderness pastures will turn green and the trees bear fruit.
God will give the early and latter rain in due measure.
The floors will be full of grain and the vats will overflow.
God will restore the years eaten by the devourers.
The people will eat in abundance and praise the Lord.
God is in Israel's midst and the people will not be put to shame.

joel-joel-01-gafanhotos-e-juizo.context: Joel speaks to a people who saw the land ravaged by locusts. In this passage, God promises to restore the lost years, to be among the people and to pour out his Spirit.
joel-joel-01-gafanhotos-e-juizo.focusQuestion: Facing a loss you cannot repair, what changes when you remember that God promises to be present?
joel-joel-01-gafanhotos-e-juizo.keywordGloss: An insect that devours the harvest; in the text, the plague is called a great army sent by God.
facts: God promises to restore the years eaten by the devourers.
The people will eat in abundance and praise the name of the Lord.
God declares that he is in Israel's midst.
God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh.
Signs in the sun and moon come before the great Day of the Lord.
A mighty and countless nation came against the land.

joel-joel-02-derramarei-o-meu-esp.context: After announcing restoration to the people, Joel brings the book's greatest promise: God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh, leaving out no male or female servants.
joel-joel-02-derramarei-o-meu-esp.focusQuestion: Whom do you tend to leave out when you think of who God reaches, and what does Joel 2 change in that?
joel-joel-02-derramarei-o-meu-esp.keywordGloss: God's verb in the promise: he is the one who pours out the Spirit, abundantly and on his own initiative.
facts: God will pour out the Spirit on all flesh.
Sons and daughters will prophesy.
Old men will dream and young men will see visions.
Male and female servants will also receive the Spirit.
God will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth.
The sun will turn to darkness before the Day of the Lord.

joel-joel-03-desafio-joel.context: This challenge reviews Joel: the loss from the plague, the call to tear the heart and the promise of restored years and the Spirit poured out on all flesh.
joel-joel-03-desafio-joel.focusQuestion: Facing Joel's judgment, call and promise, what is your next sincere step before God?
joel-joel-03-desafio-joel.keywordGloss: A great and terrible Day when God judges, calls the people back and acts to save.
reflectionPrompts: A loss that calls us to listen
facts: What the caterpillar left, the locust ate, in a chain.
The Day of the Lord is great and very terrible.
Joel says to tear the heart and not the garments.
God will restore the years eaten by the devourers.
The people will eat in abundance and praise the Lord.
God will pour out the Spirit on all flesh.
